Plant Parenthood’s Easy-Care Plant Guide
A simple guide to keeping your plants thriving!
________________


1. Pothos (Epipremnum aureum)
Light: Thrives in low to bright indirect light. Avoid direct sunlight, which can scorch leaves.
Water: Allow soil to dry out between waterings. Water when top 1-2 inches of soil are dry.
Humidity: Prefers moderate to high humidity but tolerates normal room conditions.
Soil: Well-draining potting mix.
Fertilizer: Feed monthly with diluted liquid fertilizer in spring and summer.
Common Issues & Solutions:
* Yellow Leaves → Overwatering. Let soil dry before watering again. Ensure pot has drainage.
* Brown, Crispy Leaves → Underwatering or low humidity. Increase watering frequency and mist occasionally.
* Leggy Growth → Not enough light. Move to a brighter spot. Trim back stems to encourage bushier growth.
________________


2. Spider Plant (Chlorophytum comosum)
Light: Prefers bright, indirect light but tolerates low light.
Water: Water when the top inch of soil is dry. Avoid soggy soil.
Humidity: Adaptable, but enjoys occasional misting.
Soil: Well-draining potting mix.
Fertilizer: Every 2-4 weeks in growing seasons (spring & summer).
Common Issues & Solutions:
* Brown Leaf Tips → Fluoride or chlorine in tap water. Use filtered or distilled water.
* Wilting Leaves → Overwatering or root rot. Allow soil to dry out and ensure proper drainage.
* Lack of “Spiderettes” (Baby Plants) → Needs more light or fertilizer. Move to a brighter spot and feed monthly.
________________


3. Christmas Cactus (Schlumbergera spp.)
Light: Bright, indirect light. Avoid prolonged direct sun.
Water: Water when top 1-2 inches of soil are dry. Keep soil slightly moist during blooming.
Humidity: Prefers high humidity; mist or use a pebble tray.
Soil: Well-draining cactus or succulent mix.
Fertilizer: Use a balanced fertilizer every month in spring and summer. Reduce feeding in fall and winter.
Common Issues & Solutions:
* Shriveled or Wrinkled Leaves → Underwatering. Increase watering but avoid waterlogging.
* Dropping Buds → Sudden temperature changes or too much movement. Keep in a stable environment.
* Red/Purple-Tinted Leaves → Too much direct sunlight. Move to filtered light.
________________


4. Philodendron (Philodendron spp.)
Light: Thrives in medium to bright indirect light. Avoid prolonged direct sun.
Water: Water when the top inch of soil is dry.
Humidity: Prefers moderate to high humidity but tolerates normal indoor levels.
Soil: Well-draining potting mix.
Fertilizer: Feed monthly during growing season with a diluted liquid fertilizer.
Common Issues & Solutions:
* Yellow Leaves → Overwatering. Let soil dry out before watering again.
* Droopy Leaves → Can indicate both overwatering and underwatering. Check soil moisture before adjusting.
* Leggy Growth → Needs more light. Move closer to a bright window.
________________


5. Jade Plant (Crassula ovata)
Light: Prefers bright, indirect light. Some direct sun is beneficial.
Water: Water deeply but infrequently. Allow soil to dry out completely between waterings.
Humidity: Low humidity preferred.
Soil: Well-draining succulent or cactus mix.
Fertilizer: Fertilize every 2-3 months in growing season.
Common Issues & Solutions:
* Wrinkled or Shriveling Leaves → Underwatering. Water thoroughly but let dry before next watering.
* Soft, Mushy Leaves → Overwatering. Check for root rot and reduce watering.
* Leggy Growth → Insufficient light. Move to a sunnier location.
________________


6. Monstera (Monstera deliciosa)
Light: Bright, indirect light. Can tolerate low light but grows slower.
Water: Water when the top 2 inches of soil are dry.
Humidity: Prefers high humidity. Mist occasionally.
Soil: Well-draining potting mix with added perlite.
Fertilizer: Every 2 weeks in spring/summer; reduce in winter.
Common Issues & Solutions:
* Yellow Leaves → Overwatering. Ensure proper drainage.
* Brown Leaf Edges → Low humidity. Increase misting or use a humidifier.
* Small or No Fenestrations (Leaf Holes) → Not enough light. Move to a brighter spot.
________________


7. Pencil Cactus (Euphorbia tirucalli)
Light: Needs bright, direct sunlight. Best near a sunny window.
Water: Water sparingly. Allow soil to dry out completely before watering.
Humidity: Low humidity preferred.
Soil: Well-draining succulent or cactus mix.
Fertilizer: Every 2 months in spring/summer.
Common Issues & Solutions:
* Drooping or Wrinkled Stems → Underwatering. Give a deep soak and let dry completely.
* Soft, Mushy Stems → Overwatering or root rot. Cut back on watering and check for rotted roots.

﻿Plant Parenthood began operating in Fall 2022, under a bed in the Eringhaus Dormitories at UNC Chapel Hill. The early focus was on planting and growing plants. During 2023, the business began honing its pop-up sale model, launched its Instagram, and gained recognition from The Daily Tar Heel. One of its campus sales sold out, becoming its biggest campus sale at the time. The team also developed its products around the needs of college students, focusing on hardy, low-maintenance indoor plants suited to dorms and other small spaces, paired with unique and sustainably sourced or reused planters.
In 2024, Plant Parenthood placed 2nd in the inaugural Joan and Chester Luby Pitch Competition and subsequently participated in Seed Money, a televised student venture pitch competition. The company also secured paid opportunities with UNC Kenan-Flagler Business School for its Earth Day initiative and UNC for a retirement party. The team later achieved its first autonomous sale, demonstrating that its sales and fulfillment systems could operate without direct owner involvement.
In 2025, Plant Parenthood expanded its social media marketing through TikTok and Instagram and purchased a greenhouse to increase inventory for the upcoming school year. The company has also developed a sustainability focus, including repurposing bottles and other materials into planters; the venture reported diverting more than 450 bottles from landfills.
In 2026, the founder received the Gerald Unks Fellowship, a personal award whose story was connected in part to the journey of building Plant Parenthood. Plant Parenthood also received a $7,500 award supporting an international exploration of plant culture during Summer 2026.

﻿Plant B Insurance
Product Overview
Plant B Insurance is a one-time plant replacement policy. Customers pay a $3 one-time fee to receive coverage for one insured plant for 12 months from the date of purchase.
If the insured plant dies or does not survive during the coverage period due to natural causes, accidental neglect, or unforeseen issues, the customer may receive one replacement plant of the same or similar type.
Coverage
Plant B Insurance covers:
* One plant per policy
* One replacement plant per policy
* Replacement with a plant of the same or similar type
* Coverage for 12 months from the policy purchase date
* Plant death or failure to survive caused by:
   * Overwatering
   * Underwatering
   * Pests
   * Environmental stress
   * Natural causes
   * Accidental neglect
   * Other unforeseen issues
The policy is described as a “no questions asked” replacement, subject to the stated exclusions and claim requirements.
Cost and Duration
* Policy price: $3 one-time fee
* Coverage period: 12 months from purchase
* Claims allowed: One claim per insured plant
* Policies covered: One plant per policy
* Transferability: Policy is non-transferable
Exclusions
Plant B Insurance does not cover:
* Intentional harm or intentional damage to the plant
* Theft
* Loss of the plant
* Replacement of the planter
* Replacement of soil
* Replacement of plant accessories
* Plants that show visible signs of recovery when the claim is submitted
Claim Requirements
To file a claim, the customer must submit:
1. A photo of the insured plant showing its current condition
2. A brief description of the issue
3. The policy number or proof of purchase
Claims must be submitted before the policy expiration date.
Replacement Process
If a claim is approved, the customer receives one replacement plant of the same or similar type.
Replacement may be provided through:
* Pickup
* Delivery
The policy states that the replacement will be provided within 1 year, although the policy does not specify an exact replacement fulfillment timeframe after claim approval.
Important Chatbot Rules
When answering customer questions:
* Do not state that Plant B Insurance covers theft or a lost plant.
* Do not state that the policy covers the planter, soil, or accessories.
* Do not promise multiple replacements or multiple claims.
* Do not state that the policy can be transferred to another person or plant.
* Do not approve a claim based only on a customer's description; the policy requires a photo and policy number/proof of purchase.
* Do not guarantee replacement if the plant shows visible signs of recovery at claim submission.
* The policy price is $3, paid once—not $3 per month.
* Coverage lasts 12 months from purchase, not indefinitely.
* “No questions asked” does not override the policy's exclusions and claim requirements.
* If the policy does not specify an answer, do not invent a policy term. Direct the customer to support: [support email/phone].
Example Customer Intent Mapping
“My plant died.”
→ Potentially covered if it occurred during the 12-month coverage period and does not fall under an exclusion. The customer must submit a photo, description, and policy number/proof of purchase.
“I overwatered my plant and it died.”
→ Overwatering is listed as a covered cause.
“I forgot to water my plant.”
→ Underwatering/accidental neglect is listed as covered.
“My plant has pests.”
→ Pests are listed as a covered cause if the plant does not survive.
“Someone stole my plant.”
→ Theft is excluded.
“I lost my plant.”
→ Loss of the plant is excluded.
“Can I get a new pot too?”
→ No. The policy covers the replacement plant, not the planter, soil, or accessories.
“Can I claim twice?”
→ No. Each policy allows one claim/replacement per insured plant.
“Can I transfer my policy?”
→ No. Policies are non-transferable.
“My plant is recovering. Can I still claim?”
→ The policy excludes plants showing visible signs of recovery at the time of claim submission.
“How much does Plant B Insurance cost?”
→ $3 one-time fee.
“How long am I covered?”
→ 12 months from the date of purchase.
“What do I need to file a claim?”
→ A photo showing the plant's condition, a brief description of the issue, and the policy number or proof of purchase.

CHATBOT ACCURACY RULES
• Do not invent plant varieties, bottle brands, prices, sizes, or availability that are not listed in this source.
• Do not claim a specific plant has a specific price unless the customer has also specified the planter category.
• Do not imply that every listed plant is available in every planter size.
• When discussing plant suitability, use the examples provided in this catalog rather than guaranteeing compatibility.
• The Xtra Large planter price is a range of $25–$30, not a fixed $25 or $30 price.
• A custom order costs $45.
• Custom container requests are subject to feasibility. Do not guarantee that a requested container can be sourced.
• A TikTok feature for custom orders is a potential opportunity, not a guaranteed benefit.
• If a customer asks about a plant, bottle, price, or option not covered by this source, do not make up an answer. Direct the customer to Plant Parenthood for confirmation.
